questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: This exchange was part of a summer school held annually in the same city, so I did not necessarily choose the destination myself. However, I would say that the city is quite special if you are interested in muscle physiology, as it is home to several internationally recognized research groups working in the fields of skeletal muscle biology, neuromuscular disorders, exercise physiology, and muscle regeneration. The city also hosts a strong network of academic and clinical institutions that contribute significantly to muscle research.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration process for the summer school was very straightforward. Once you receive your letter of acceptance, you are invited to an introductory webinar where all the necessary practical information is provided. During the webinar, the organizers explain the next steps of the process, identify the relevant contact persons, and outline any information or documents that participants are required to submit. Overall, the process was well organized and easy to follow.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You had access to the contact details of both the organizers and the administrative staff.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It is difficult to say, as this was organized as a one week summer school rather than a traditional 6 month exchange or study-abroad program. The organizers had incorporated several social activities throughout the week, including a guided city tour, which provided opportunities for participants to interact and get to know one another outside the academic setting. With that said we still had symposia that were very similar to lectures at UCPH. With that said, we still attended symposia that were very similar in format to the lectures I am familiar with at UCPH.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. You should not expect to do a lot of studying  on coursework from Denmark during the summer school, as the programme is very intensive. Activities typically began at 8:00 a.m. and often continued until we returned to our hotel rooms around 22:00-23:00 
2. As mentioned, the days are very long, so I would recommend bringing an extra lunch, as well as snacks
3. Take advantage of the opportunity to interact with both the invited researchers and the other participants. The summer school brings together students and scientists from different countries and backgrounds, making it an great opportunity to expand your professional network.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't worry about potential language barriers. Everyone speaks excellent English.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The most rewarding aspect of the summer school was the combination of hands-on practical exercises and scientific symposia. The practical sessions provided access to equipment and experimental techniques that bachelor students may not normally have the opportunity to use, while the symposia offered the chance to learn directly from renowned researchers in the field.
